Ki-67, 1p36 loss and 9p21/CDKN2A loss as prognostic factors in skull base chordoma

Systematic review and meta-analysis: complete analysis report

Author

Cássio da Silva Minuzzo, Pedro Malfussi Horst, Nicolas de Cesaro Schpchacki, Francisco Martins Lamas, Francisco Ratto Fabris, Erion Junior de Andrade

Published

27 October 2026

This report reproduces every analysis of the systematic review and meta-analysis registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261390460). All pooled estimates, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, small-study-effect tests and forest plots are recomputed from data/estimates.csv by R/meta_analysis.R each time the report is rendered. The numbers therefore always reflect the current dataset. Tables can be filtered, sorted and copied.

HR, hazard ratio for the higher biomarker category (binary) or per 1 percentage point of Ki-67 (continuous), with values above 1 indicating a worse prognosis. Pooled estimates come from random-effects models (restricted maximum likelihood estimate of τ²) with Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman confidence intervals (ad hoc variance correction). PI, prediction interval; nr, not reported. A pooled estimate required at least three independent compatible cohorts; adjusted and unadjusted estimates and binary and continuous scales were never combined.

6 Subgroup analysis by Ki-67 cut-off

Binary Ki-67, unadjusted and derived HRs; cut-offs around 5% (4–6%) versus other values, tested with random-effects meta-regression. Subgroups with fewer than three cohorts are described without inference. The adjusted (primary) synthesis was not divided, because only one cohort used a cut-off outside 4–6%.

9 Risk of bias (QUIPS)

Each combination of study, biomarker and estimate class was assessed in six domains. Unadjusted estimates are at high risk for D5 (confounding) by rule, and their overall rating is computed without D5.

10 Certainty of evidence (GRADE)

10.1 Summary of findings

HR, hazard ratio for the higher biomarker category (binary) or per 1 percentage point (continuous); pooled estimates from random-effects models (REML) with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals (ad hoc variance correction); PI, 95% prediction interval. k, number of cohorts; n, patients; nr, not reported. Certainty of evidence rated with GRADE for prognostic factors; statements follow GRADE informative-statement guidance (low certainty, ‘may’; very low certainty, ‘the evidence is very uncertain’).
ᵃ The study’s ‘overall survival’ censored deaths from surgical complications or causes unrelated to the disease.
ᵇ 95% CI derived from the reported p value.
ᶜ Hazard ratios relative to 0–3% of cells with homozygous deletion; CIs not reported.
ᵈ Estimates published in the conference abstract (Gersey 2022) linked to the full-text report (Muthiah 2026).
ᵉ Muthiah 2026: number of patients with FISH results not reported; the cohort of 110 patients and its 18 deaths are counted.

10.2 Evidence profile

Criteria applied to all comparisons (Iorio et al., BMJ 2015; Foroutan et al., J Clin Epidemiol 2020; Guyatt et al., J Clin Epidemiol 2011; Santesso et al., J Clin Epidemiol 2020): (1) evidence from prognostic cohorts starts at high certainty; (2) risk of bias (QUIPS): −1 when most of the evidence is at high risk, −2 only when the limitation is likely to change the direction or magnitude of the effect, judged by comparing estimates with and without the limitation; (3) inconsistency: −1 for estimates in opposite directions with I² ≥50%, or when the prediction interval includes 1 while the confidence interval does not; no downgrading when estimates point in the same direction, heterogeneity is moderate and the confidence interval already includes 1; (4) imprecision: binary scale, −1 when the CI includes 1 or the total number of events is below the optimal information size (~190 events to detect HR 1.5 with 80% power and two-sided alpha 0.05, Schoenfeld formula); continuous scale, −1 when the CI of the HR per 5 points includes 1; −2 when the CI is very wide with k≤2 or fewer than ~50 events; (5) indirectness: −1 when platform, zygosity or outcome differ from the review question; (6) publication bias: tested formally only with k≥10 (funnel plot and Egger test); (7) subgroup differences with fewer than 3 studies in one level are described but not used to change certainty; (8) no upgrading when already downgraded for risk of bias.

11 Reproducibility

The report was rendered with R version 4.5.3 (2026-03-11 ucrt), metafor 4.8.0, DT 0.34.0 and ggplot2 4.0.2. To reproduce it, install R (version 4.3 or later), the packages metafor, DT, ggplot2, knitr and rmarkdown, and Quarto, then run quarto render index.qmd in the repository folder. The analysis alone can be run with Rscript R/meta_analysis.R, which writes the tables in results/.
